source_snapshot.title: Dubai Civil Defence announces colour-coded AI safety platform for buildings and more drones for firefighting
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Dubai Civil Defence is set to give property investors a live, colour-coded view of how safe their buildings are, and plans to expand its firefighting drone fleet from two to six by next year, officials told Gulf News at Dubai Future Week on Thursday.The new digital platform, called Safety Pulse for Investors, will launch in the first quarter of 2027. Authorities say it is the first of its kind in the Middle East.It uses artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) technology to feed real-time safety data directly to owners and investors..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..How it worksUntil now, the safety data on Dubai's buildings was held by Civil Defence and linked to its operations room. Now it will be shared with those who own the buildings. Investors will see everything on one dashboard. They can pass it on to their operations or maintenance engineers, who will no longer have to chase information.Each building will be colour-coded, with green signalling a healthy rating. The rating depends on factors such as maintenance records, false alarms, defects in safety systems, missed inspections and the absence of a Civil Defence safety certificate. AI will help categorise the data..Abu Dhabi deploys AI-Driven drones as first responders to emergencies and disasters.The platform tracks five systems: fire alarms, firefighting equipment, gas, electrical and lifts. It can spot faults, leaks and maintenance needs early. It can also connect owners with maintenance companies and send alerts to the Civil Defence Operations Room without human intervention.The platform is linked to all 26 fire and rescue stations in the emirate, with plans to grow to 40 stations and points in line with the Dubai 2040 Urban Master Plan.Investors will be able to see the nearest station to their property, while Civil Defence teams can anticipate incidents and speed up their response. Investors with many properties can analyse the safety risks in multiple buildings at the same time and can take preventive or corrective measures.The Safety Pulse Platform covers investment and commercial properties but not private homes. Integration with Dubai Municipality and free zone licensing data is possible in future.Safety as an economic asset“Safety and investment are two sides of the same coin,” said Afaf Jassim Al Muhairi, CEO of the General Department of Institutional Leadership and Excellence at Dubai Civil Defence. She said the aim is to move from traditional supervision to proactive prevention, protecting investments as well as lives.Lt Col Eng Taher Hassan Al Taher, director of the corporate pioneership department, said the data matters because investors need to know where they are putting their money. “He doesn’t have to ask or look for information. He will have everything on one platform,” he said..Sharjah’s Aman system monitors 13,700 buildings for fire alerts.The announcement also includes a Global Attractiveness Index, which measures how safety affects investor and tourist decisions. It rests on four pillars: future readiness (30 per cent), proactive safety (25 per cent), protection of lives and property (20 per cent) and business continuity (25 per cent).Al Taher said safety, of buildings and of places, is one of the reasons tourists and investors choose Dubai. The platform is also expected to use AI and digital twins to predict risks.More Shaheen dronesOn firefighting, Al Taher said Civil Defence currently has two Shaheen drones and expects to have six by next year, “hopefully” with updated features.The Shaheen is Dubai Civil Defence’s AI-powered firefighting drone system for high-rise buildings. It was unveiled at Intersec 2025. It carries 1,200 litres of water and firefighting foam and is designed for buildings up to 200 metres tall.It was used in September 2025 to help bring a residential building fire in Al Barsha under control. Civil Defence crews reached the scene within six minutes and no injuries were reported. An improved version was showcased in January 2026.The new features are still in research and development and will be announced later. For now, the drones are meant for high-rise buildings. The aim is to eventually reach interiors as well.Asked about challenges, Al Taher said Civil Defence is prepared and ready for any critical situation. He said no policy changes were needed after when Dubai faced attacks as part of the regional crisis, as such scenarios were already factored in.

source_verification.reason: All factual claims in the post are directly supported by the source text.

claims.claim: In the first quarter of 2027, Dubai will launch a digital platform called Safety Pulse for investors that shows a live colour-coded safety rating of buildings using AI and IoT.
The platform tracks fire alarm systems, firefighting equipment, gas, electrical, and lifts systems, and connects owners with maintenance companies and fire stations.
By 2027, the firefighting drone fleet Shaheen will increase from two to six units to fight fires in high-rise buildings.

title: Dubai Civil Defence announces colour-coded AI safety platform for buildings and more drones for firefighting
summary_ru: 🚇 Дубай запустит AI-платформу для оценки безопасности зданий 💻 В первом квартале 2027 года в Дубае появится цифровая платформа Safety Pulse для инвесторов, которая покажет в реальном времени цветовую оценку безопасности зданий с помощью искусственного интеллекта и IoT. Платформа отслеживает системы пожарной сигнализации, оборудования, газа, электричества и лифтов, а также связывает владельцев с обслуживающими компаниями и пожарными станциями. Кроме того, к 2027 году парк пожарных дронов Shaheen увеличится с двух до шести единиц для борьбы с возгораниями в высотках.
